Rows an entrant trained on count as wrong here too. Calibration error is the average gap, in points, between how confident a model said it was and how often it was right, taken over ten confidence bins; zero is perfect. The diamond on the ladder is the share of answers given with at least 95% confidence that were wrong.

How the index is computed

One number per model, from the same 38-benchmark panel. Weights are fixed; nothing is tuned to the entrants. Full methodology →

Decision Index
100 × mean of the five area scores

Each benchmark is chance-corrected first: 0 is random guessing, 100 is perfect. Each capability area is the mean of its benchmarks' primary metrics, so every area counts the same however many tasks it holds. ForecastBench counts against its baseline: always predict p = 0.5 scores zero.

Coverage counts
unanswered = wrong

Every model faces the same 120,340 requests. A request the model cannot take, refuses or errors on scores zero, so nobody climbs by skipping the hard cases.

Same cases as Jev
frozen suite · frozen answers

Jev's own results were recorded once and never re-run. On every model page each result sits beside Jev's answer on exactly the same cases.

Decision Index 0.2.1 averages 38 benchmarks in five areas. Arts & Human Taste weighs 10%; the other four share 90% in proportion to the square root of their benchmark count (knowledge 25.8%, language 25.8%, retrieval 20.0%, tools 18.3%). Inside an area, gold ★ benchmarks weigh 1.2 and the rest 1.0; the index is 100 x the weighted mean of the five areas. Each benchmark is chance-corrected first, (score - chance) / (1 - chance) clipped to 0-1, so 0 means random guessing and 100 means perfect. Every score is coverage-adjusted, so an unanswered or unsupported request counts as wrong. ForecastBench enters against its baseline: clip((0.25 - Brier) / 0.25) x coverage, so always predicting 0.5 scores zero. MMLU, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, RouterBench, SGD stay on the board as non-index benchmarks. The six interactive environments are still unrun and stay out. Every entrant on the board has results on all 38 index benchmarks. Point estimates only, no uncertainty intervals yet.
